Harvesting from the Land & Creating a Maker’s Kit 
Crafting for Survival
Travelers exploring the primal wilds of Sol'Kesh journey into lands that have never known the step of an intelligent being for eons, to deal 
with such a natural setting, the many of amenities and supplies needed to survive must be crafted in the field, and by their own hands. 
Crafting in Sol'Kesh does not rely on villages, merchants or a bustling economy, but instead on the Travelers Knowledge, Components, 
and Time to create what they want from the bounties of the natural environment and creatures within.
The Maker's Kit
Self sufficiency is key to survival, and the Maker's Kit allows a 
Traveler to craft far away from the trappings of civilization. While 
not of infinite use, the Makers' Kit accounts for the mundane 
resources needed to craft the unique items of Sol'Kesh. No 
Maker's Kit looks alike, whether it is a leather satchel filled to the 
brim with odds and ends, or a sturdy wooden cabinet with an 
organized set of tools, the Maker's Kit is truly a representation of 
the Travelers own sense of style and organization.
Creating or Resupplying a Maker's Kit 
The wilds of Sol'Kesh are nothing if not bountiful, and all that a 
Traveler needs to create or resupply a Maker's Kit is available with 
the right amount of time and cunning. 
• A Traveler may spend 1 day foraging in any biome, alone or in 
a party to craft their own Maker's Kit or replenish their current 
Maker's Kits Supply Charges. 
• The wilds are never safe when rummaging for supplies, at the 
end of the day, the Keeper rolls on the Scavengers Table of the 
specific biome that the Travelers are in. If any creature results are 
rolled, immediately begin a combat encounter. 
• If the Travelers survive the encounter, they then roll a 1d8, adding 
their Wisdom (Survival) Modifier, this result is the amount of 
Supply Charges they receive for their Maker's Kit. A Maker's 
Kit has a max amount of Supply Charges equal to 4 times the 
Traveler's Proficiency Bonus.
• Maker's Kits and their use are personal to a Traveler, and its 
recommended that they may not be shared among other Traveler's 
and cannot be sold. 
Crafting Notes
There are seven key elements to consider when using Crafting. 
 
• Maker's Kits have a set of Supply Charges that are expended 
through use. When a Maker's Kit has zero Supply Charges it 
cannot be used, but it is not destroyed, it is simple empty. 
• Whether success or failure, the time needed for crafting is spent.
• If an item requires multiple days of crafter, whether Focused or 
Patient, the days need not be consecutive.
• The following Tools are readily available within the Maker's kit to 
create any items that require:
  Artisan Tools
  Alchemist's Supplies
  Brewer's Supplies
  Carpenter's Tools
  Cobbler's Tools
  Glassblower's Tools
  Leatherworker's Tools
  Potter's Tools
  Smith's Tools
  Weaver's Tools
  Woodcarver's Tools 
• While the Tools needed to craft are automatically supplied, 
the Proficiency to use the specific Tools are still required for the 
Traveler to know. Having the specific Tool Proficiency adds a 
bonus to the Crafting roll. 
• Failing to reach the DC of the crafted item will result in the time 
needed to craft being spent. Failing a second time will result in the 
Components being destroyed.
• When a Traveler is ready to craft, they roll a 1d20 and consult the 
chart below for added modifiers to their roll.
Upon slaying or chancing upon the corpse of a creature, 
every Traveler present will have an opportunity to Scavenge 
it for Components, this can take the form of a Survival check 
when harvesting directly from the body, or a Nature check 
when searching nearby for eggs or other cast off items. It is 
recommended that the Keeper describe the components that may 
be Scavenged from the carcass without mentioning the Difficulty 
Class (DC) of the roll.
• A Keeper should mention what components are available as a 
Traveler must mention which Component they wish to Scavenge 
before attempting the roll. 
• The corpse of each creature or defeated swarm may be attempted 
to be Scavenged for a total of 3 times, while apex creatures are a 
total of 6, regardless of which Traveler has attempted it.
• Creatures found one hour after their death will not yield any 
Consumable Components. A Traveler may ascertain the age 
of a corpse by doing a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom 
(Survival) check.
• Failures to Scavenge are not to be taken likely, as the spilled blood 
and time spent harvesting within the wilds of Sol'Kesh may attract 
carrion. If attempts to Scavenge a creature result in two failures 
in a row, the Keeper must then roll on the Scavengers Table of the 
specific biome that the Travelers are in, and if any creature results 
are rolled, immediately begin a combat encounter. 
Knowledge
The flora and fauna of Sol'Kesh have adapted unique forms to 
thrive within their ecological niches. Unless a Traveler wants to 
test the toxicity of every mushroom they come across the hard 
(and potentially lethal) way, many of these natural Resources 
require deep, careful study to discover their potential use. A 
Traveler may gain this wisdom either through discovering written 
texts or recipes, discussing with knowledgeable NPCs or studying 
it themselves. A Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Knowledge) 
check can ascertain what kind of items may be created with any 
given Component. For Scavenged Components, the DC is the 
same as the Scavenging DC found on the creature's stat block. 
While foraged, fished or trapped Components are set to DC 10. 
Components
Sol'Kesh's crafted items are unique, rather primitive, never 
seen before amalgamations of gathered resources and animalr 
remains. The Components needed per item are listed on their 
Crafting Guide (pg. 260). These Components can be found in a 
multitude of ways befitting the Keeper's story, but an ambitious 
and self-reliant Traveler may obtain what they need by Hunting, 
Foraging, Setting Snares, Scavenging and Fishing.

Time
From a hastily chipped arrowhead to a finely crafted set of armor, 
creation takes time. 
Time spent crafting can take the form of either:
• Focused Crafting - Actions such as hammering copper, carving 
bone, anything that takes active effort to perform is considered 
Focused Crafting as this leaves little else to do but the task at hand. 
• Patient Crafting - Once prepared, many items take time before 
they are ready to be used. Brews ferment, water-logged coral dries, 
glue dries and many others simply take days to set. A Traveler can 
craft during their rests over many days of adventuring, hideaway 
their items as it readies, or spend time during downtime to 
prepare many long term items.
